keywords_en: Criminal; Embezzlement; Second Instance; Intermediate People's Court; Beijing; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Determination of Intent for Embezzlement; Determination of Public Property; Determination of Taking Advantage of One's Position; Reversal of Judgment; Use of Research Funds; Development of Magnetic Therapy Products; Non-duty Technical Achievement
full_text_en:
Case of Declaration of Yuan Zhonghua's Innocence

Defendant: Yuan Zhonghua, male, 50 years old, former engineer at the Precision Alloy Research Department of the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute (subsequently Vice Chairman and General Manager of China Bioengineering Company, a subsidiary of China International Trust and Investment Corporation). Arrested on September 14, 1985.

In the case of Yuan Zhonghua charged with corruption, the Beijing Haidian District People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution before the Haidian District People's Court. The Haidian District People's Court conducted an open trial in accordance with the law and found the following:

During his tenure at the Precision Alloy Research Department (hereinafter referred to as the "Precision Research Department"), from May 1982 to February 1983, while responsible for the collaborative development of magnetic therapy caps with the Beijing Cap Factory, Yuan Zhonghua, by taking advantage of his position, appropriated for himself one set of a Japanese "Yashica" brand 135-type camera and accessories, purchased with experimental funds, valued at RMB 2,046.40. Thereafter, Yuan Zhonghua, together with Li Yuguo (separately prosecuted), used experimental funds to purchase two "Ricoh" brand cameras with two sets of accessories, and, under the guise of purchasing electronic components, purchased two Japanese "Sharp" brand 6060-type stereo cassette recorders. Yuan Zhonghua received one "Ricoh" camera and accessories set and one "Sharp" 6060-type stereo cassette recorder, with a total value of RMB 2,423.34.

From February 1983 to November 1984, Yuan Zhonghua, together with Li Yuguo, in the name of the Precision Research Department, entered into a research protocol agreement with the Beijing Haidian District Yongfeng Industrial Company for the development of magnetic therapy health bras. During this period, Yuan Zhonghua, by taking advantage of his position, used research funds to purchase one color TV monitor, one Japanese "Sharp" GE-777-type double-cassette stereo recorder, one BT-11 recorder, three micro-recorders, one "Rowa" blender, one English typewriter, two negative ion generators, one digital multimeter, and one black briefcase, totaling RMB 7,216, which he appropriated for himself.

In January 1985, Yuan Zhonghua, by taking advantage of his position, withdrew RMB 4,000 from the RMB 6,000 temporarily deposited by his unit at the Xuzhou Medical Science Research Institute in Jiangsu Province, and appropriated it for himself.

Through the above means, Yuan Zhonghua embezzled public funds and property totaling RMB 15,685.74. After the incident, the above illicit funds and property, except for the RMB 4,000 and one "Sharp" 6060-type stereo cassette recorder, were all recovered.

The Haidian District People's Court held that the defendant, Yuan Zhonghua, as a state functionary, took advantage of his position to embezzle public funds and property intended for scientific research, in a large amount, thereby constituting the crime of corruption as stipulated in Article 155, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Considering the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of social harm of Yuan Zhonghua's crime, even the minimum statutory punishment was deemed too severe. Pursuant to Article 59, paragraph 2, of the Criminal Law, and upon decision by the Adjudication Committee, punishment could be imposed below the statutory minimum. In accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, all property illegally obtained by Yuan Zhonghua should be recovered. Accordingly, on May 28, 1987, the Haidian District People's Court sentenced Yuan Zhonghua to three years' imprisonment for the crime of corruption and ordered the recovery of the seized illicit property.

The defendant, Yuan Zhonghua, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Beijing Intermediate People's Court, arguing that the facts found in the original judgment did not correspond with the actual circumstances and that his conduct did not constitute a crime.

Upon retrial, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court found the following:

From May 1982 to February 1983, at the request of the Beijing Cap Factory and the Beijing Haidian District Yongfeng Industrial Company, the appellant Yuan Zhonghua entered into agreements with them for the development of magnetic therapy health caps and magnetic therapy health bras. The agreements stipulated that the Cap Factory would provide RMB 30,000, of which RMB 5,000 would be transferred to the Precision Research Department for mold making, provision of test magnetic sheets, and other expenses, while the remainder would be kept with the Cap Factory for expenses including research group and hospital clinical trials, instrument purchases, travel, health subsidies, and technical allowances. The Yongfeng Industrial Company provided RMB 54,000, of which RMB 3,000 would be transferred to the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute as scientific research fees, and the remainder would be temporarily held by Yongfeng Industrial Company on behalf. After the agreements were concluded, the seal was affixed by Li Yuguo, Deputy Office Director of the Precision Research Department. Li Yuguo believed that, under the agreements, the funds transferred to the Precision Research Department would be managed by that department; the funds held in custody by the factory, being not subject to the control of the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute, would not be interfered with by the Precision Research Department and would be managed by Yuan Zhonghua. Yuan Zhonghua believed that, regarding the RMB 8,000 transferred to the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute, under the Institute's then-unwritten rule—whereby researchers collaborating with external entities needed to pay the Institute between RMB 2,000 and RMB 6,000—such payment permitted them to occupy working hours and receive corresponding compensation.

During the performance of the contracts, except for over RMB 30,000 still held in custody by Yongfeng Industrial Company before the incident, the remaining over RMB 40,000 was used by Yuan Zhonghua for research work and for the establishment of a magnetic therapy medical laboratory. From July 1982 to early 1984, Yuan Zhonghua successively purchased items worth over RMB 14,000 using research funds, including, for the study of music therapy, seven recorders of various models; for the study of psychological therapy and the influence of audio-visual feedback on human emotions, one color TV monitor; and for other studies, three imported cameras with three sets of accessories, two negative ion generators, one blender, one English typewriter, and one digital multimeter. Due to the lack of a fixed experimental location, the above items, except for one camera and one recorder temporarily placed in Li Yuguo's home, were all temporarily stored in Yuan Zhonghua's own home. Yuan Zhonghua purchased these items and placed them in his home, informing relevant leaders, and some of the items were even used at the original unit. In March 1985, Yuan Zhonghua's employer, China Bioengineering Technology Development Company, was placed under China International Trust and Investment Corporation and renamed China Bioengineering Company. In July of the same year, Yuan Zhonghua repeatedly stated to the company's vice general manager and others that the above items could be provided for the company's use.

After signing the contracts, Yuan Zhonghua actively worked in accordance with the agreements and completed the research tasks ahead of schedule. In April 1983 and March 1984, after evaluations by experts from over ten hospitals, including the General Hospital of the People's Liberation Army, the magnetic therapy caps and magnetic therapy bras were deemed to have "good therapeutic effects" and were recommended for mass production.

In the second half of 1983, with the approval of the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute leadership, the Biomedical Engineering Materials Technology Service Department (hereinafter referred to as the "Bio-Medical Department") was established, tasked with providing biomedical technical services externally, with self-raised funds. Yuan Zhonghua served as the Chief Engineer of this department. After its establishment, Xu Guoxiang, an engineer from the Xuzhou Magnetic Materials Factory in Jiangsu Province (formerly an engineer at the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute), requested Yuan Zhonghua to purchase magnetic sheets produced by that factory. After purchasing and screening them, Yuan Zhonghua sold the qualified magnetic sheets to Yongfeng Industrial Company at the price set by the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute, thereby accumulating RMB 20,000 for the Bio-Medical Department. In May 1984, due to work needs and with leadership approval, the Bio-Medical Department remitted RMB 6,000 from the above funds to the Xuzhou Medical Science Research Institute in Jiangsu Province. In August 1984, the China Bioengineering Technology Development Company was established, with Yuan Zhonghua as General Manager, and the funds of the former Bio-Medical Department were transferred to this company. In January 1985, Yuan Zhonghua led a team to Anhui to negotiate the establishment of the Huangshan Rehabilitation Center with local hospitals. Passing through Xuzhou, due to insufficient funds, without completing necessary financial procedures, he withdrew RMB 4,000 from the RMB 6,000 temporarily deposited at the Xuzhou Medical Science Research Institute for use as operational expenses.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, statements of the defendant, documentary evidence, and physical evidence.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court held that:

(1) Yuan Zhonghua lacked the intent to embezzle. The research protocols Yuan Zhonghua signed with the Beijing Cap Factory and the Yongfeng Industrial Company provided that the research funds were supplied by the other party and could be freely disposed of, with all expenditure accounts managed by the other party. If Yuan Zhonghua had the intent to embezzle, he would not have had the other party manage the expenditure accounts. Yuan Zhonghua used the funds for research and fulfilled the tasks stipulated in the agreements, clearly lacking the intent to embezzle.

(2) Yuan Zhonghua's conduct was not harmful to society. A crime must be an act harmful to society and subject to criminal punishment. The magnetic therapy caps and magnetic therapy bras developed by Yuan Zhonghua were, according to expert evaluations, scientifically sound research results with good therapeutic effects. Yuan Zhonghua's research on magnetic therapy constituted pioneering scientific exploration, generating not only positive economic and social benefits but also attracting attention from foreign scholars. His conduct was beneficial to society, the people, the development of productive forces, and the advancement of science and technology. The magnetic therapy health bra developed by Yuan Zhonghua had been applied for a non-service invention utility model patent in his own name, which had been approved by the Patent Office of the People's Republic of China.

(3) The research funds used by Yuan Zhonghua were funds provided by the other party, not public property. The entrusted technology development contracts Yuan Zhonghua signed with the relevant entities, under the objective conditions at the time, were essentially contracts between Yuan Zhonghua personally and the other party, even though they bore the seal of the Precision Research Department (which did not have independent legal personality). In his magnetic therapy development activities, except for purchasing magnetic sheets from the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute through normal channels, Yuan Zhonghua did not use any material or technical equipment of the Institute; he conducted the activities entirely independently using funds provided by the other party. As for the occupation of normal working hours, Yuan Zhonghua had paid several thousand yuan to the Central Iron and Steel Research Institute as compensation. Therefore, Yuan Zhonghua's technological development achievements should be regarded as non-service technological achievements. The original trial court's treatment of the use of research funds as public property and its finding that Yuan Zhonghua committed the crime of corruption were improper.

(4) In the process of engaging in magnetic therapy research, Yuan Zhonghua had the right, under the agreements, to control and use the funds provided by the manufacturers; there was no premise of taking advantage of his position. Yuan Zhonghua purchased, stored, and used the purchased equipment, repeatedly informing relevant leaders truthfully, and did not employ any illegal means. As for the RMB 4,000 Yuan Zhonghua withdrew, it was used for business dealings and social activities, and the failure to complete necessary financial procedures constituted a violation of financial regulations, but should not be treated as a crime.

In summary, Yuan Zhonghua, in order to develop and research magnetic therapy biomedical engineering technology, signed entrusted technology development contracts with relevant entities, independently conducted magnetic therapy technology research, and obtained certain technological achievements. His conduct conformed to the current science and technology regulations and policies of the state. The original trial court's imposition of criminal liability on Yuan Zhonghua for the crime of corruption was improper and should be corrected.

Accordingly, on April 9, 1988, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 136, item (2), of the Criminal Procedure Law, rendered the following judgment:

1. Set aside the criminal judgment (86) Xing Zi No. 150 of the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing dated May 28, 1987;

2. Declare Yuan Zhonghua not guilty.
